        (3) equal mix of synchronous and asynchronous affordances (i.e., helldivers 2),
        (4) mostly asynchronous with few synchronous affordances (i.e. cookie clicker),
        (5) entirely asynchronous (i.e., chess by postage mail)
reasoning: The study describes an online learning system for individuals with developmental disabilities. The system is web-based, which implies it can be accessed asynchronously. However, there are mentions of real-time interactions and feedback, such as audio-based positive reinforcers and progress information shown while the activity is in progress. This suggests that while the system is mostly asynchronous, there are some synchronous affordances, such as real-time feedback and progress tracking. The mention of lagging and slow input detection due to internet connection issues further supports the idea that the system relies on real-time interactions to some extent.
